workflow.critical: The workflow execution engine is governed by: {project-root}/_bmad/core/tasks/workflow.xml
You MUST have already loaded and processed: {installed_path}/workflow.yaml
Communicate all responses in {communication_language} and language MUST be tailored to {user_skill_level}
Linear is the single source of truth - read story context from Linear issue description
Execute ALL steps in exact order; do NOT skip steps

Absolutely DO NOT stop because of "milestones", "significant progress", or "session boundaries". Continue in a single execution until the story is COMPLETE (all ACs satisfied and all tasks checked) UNLESS a HALT condition is triggered or the USER gives other instruction.
Do NOT schedule a "next session" or request review pauses unless a HALT condition applies.
User skill level ({user_skill_level}) affects conversation style ONLY, not code updates.

After completing each step, you MUST call `gt mol step done <step-id>` with a detailed --body. This posts a progress comment to the Linear issue and tracks molecule completion. Do NOT skip this — it is the primary mechanism for reporting progress.

step.action: Load {{linear_mapping_file}} to get team_id and project_id

check.if: linear_mapping_file does not exist OR team_id is empty
check.output: Linear mapping not initialized. Run sprint-planning first to configure Linear integration.

step.action: Query Linear for ready stories (Todo status): mcp__linear__list_issues with team={{team_id}}, project={{project_id}}, label="BMAD-Managed", state="Todo"
Filter results to only include stories (exclude parent epic issues by checking for "[Epic-" prefix)
Sort results by title to get ordered story keys

check.if: no ready stories found in Linear
check.output:
No stories with "Todo" status found in Linear.
**Options:** 1. Run `create-story` to add Dev Notes to the next backlog story 2. Check if stories are "In Progress" (may need to resume work) 3. Run `sprint-planning` to see current status

step.action: Parse first result title to extract story key: "[1-2-name] Title" -> "1-2-name"
Store {{linear_issue_id}} from query result
If {{linear_issue_id}} not set, query Linear to find issue: mcp__linear__list_issues with team={{team_id}}, project={{project_id}}, label="BMAD-Managed", query="[{{story_key}}]"
Store {{linear_issue_id}} from query result
Get full issue details: mcp__linear__get_issue with id={{linear_issue_id}}

Parse issue description to extract: - Story statement (As a/I want/So that) - Acceptance Criteria - Dev Notes section (Architecture Guidance, Technical Requirements, Testing Requirements, etc.) - Implementation Tasks with checkboxes

action.if: no Dev Notes section found in description
action.output: Story [{{story_key}}] does not have Dev Notes. Run `create-story` first.
action.action: Load comprehensive context from Dev Notes section of Linear issue description
Extract developer guidance: architecture requirements, previous learnings, technical specifications
Load {project_context} for coding standards and project-wide patterns (if exists)
Parse Implementation Tasks to identify first incomplete task (unchecked [ ])
Get comments on Linear issue: mcp__linear__list_comments with issueId={{linear_issue_id}}
Check for code review comments (containing "Code Review" or "Review Findings")

check.if: code review comment exists with unresolved items
check.action: Extract action items from review comment

action.action:
Run: gt mol step done load-context --body "## Context Loaded
**Story:** [{{story_key}}] **Linear Issue:** {{linear_issue_id}} **Requirements:** [story statement and acceptance criteria] **Acceptance Criteria:** [list all AC from issue] **Key Files:** [relevant files identified from Dev Notes] **Review Continuation:** [yes/no, with details if yes]"

step.goal: Set up working branch and mark in-progress
step.action: Check current branch state: git status, git branch --show-current
If not on a feature branch, create one: git checkout -b polecat/{{agent_name}} or feature/{{story_key}}
Ensure clean working state: git status (should show "working tree clean")

Run: gt mol step done branch-setup --body "## Branch Setup
**Branch:** [branch-name] **Base:** {{default_branch}} at [commit-sha] **Status:** Clean working tree, rebased on latest"

step.goal: Verify tests pass before starting work
step.critical: Check if the codebase is healthy BEFORE starting your work
step.action: Determine how to run tests for this repo (infer test framework from project structure)
Run the full test suite to establish a baseline

check.action: Good - codebase is healthy, proceed to planning
Determine if failures are pre-existing (not caused by your changes)
If pre-existing: note the failures and proceed with your work
Do NOT fix pre-existing failures - that is not your assignment

step.action:
Run: gt mol step done preflight-tests --body "## Preflight Tests
**Result:** PASS/FAIL **Test command:** [command used] **Notes:** [any pre-existing issues found]"

step.goal: Design implementation approach before writing code
step.critical: Plan your approach BEFORE writing code. A good plan prevents wasted work.
step.action: Re-read the issue carefully - review all Implementation Tasks from Dev Notes
Identify acceptance criteria and constraints
Explore the codebase: - Find the relevant files and understand existing patterns - Identify where changes need to go - Look for similar features you can follow as examples

Design your approach: - List the files you'll modify/create - Outline the key changes in each file - Identify potential risks or unknowns - Plan the red-green-refactor cycle for each task - Decide on test strategy (what to test, how)
Verify feasibility: - Can you implement this within your assignment scope? - Are there dependencies you're missing? - Does your approach follow existing conventions from Dev Notes?

action.if: scope is larger than expected or blockers discovered

step.action: HALT and request guidance

Run: gt mol step done plan --body "## Plan
**Files to modify:** - path/to/file1 - description of changes - path/to/file2 - description of changes
**Approach:** [detailed description of what you'll do and how, including task order]
**Tests:** [what you'll test and how, red-green-refactor strategy]"

step.goal: Implement all tasks following red-green-refactor cycle
step.critical: FOLLOW THE IMPLEMENTATION TASKS FROM LINEAR ISSUE EXACTLY AS WRITTEN - NO DEVIATION
Execute continuously without pausing until all tasks complete or explicit HALT condition
step.action: Review the current task from the Linear issue Dev Notes - this is your authoritative implementation guide
Write FAILING tests first for the task functionality
Confirm tests fail before implementation - this validates test correctness
Implement MINIMAL code to make tests pass
Run tests to confirm they now pass
Handle error conditions and edge cases as specified in task
Improve code structure while keeping tests green
Ensure code follows architecture patterns from Dev Notes
Verify ALL tests for this task ACTUALLY EXIST and PASS 100%
Confirm implementation matches EXACTLY what the task specifies
Run full test suite to ensure NO regressions introduced

check.action: DO NOT mark task complete - fix issues first
HALT if unable to fix validation failures

step.action: Note task as completed, track files created/modified
Commit the completed task: git add [files] git commit -m "[type]: [description] ([story_key])"

action.if: new dependencies required beyond story specifications

step.action: HALT: "Additional dependencies need user approval"
HALT and request guidance
HALT: "Cannot proceed without necessary configuration files"
Determine if more incomplete tasks remain in Implementation Tasks list
step.critical: NEVER implement anything not in the Implementation Tasks from Linear issue
NEVER proceed to next task until current task is complete AND tests pass
step.action:
Run: gt mol step done implement --body "## Implementation Complete
**Changes:** - path/to/file1 - what was changed - path/to/file2 - what was changed
**Commits:** [list of commits made]
**Tasks completed:** [count] of [total] **Notes:** [any decisions, trade-offs, or issues]"

step.goal: Self-review all changes before final testing
step.action: Review the full diff: git diff origin/{{default_branch}}...HEAD
Review all commits: git log --oneline origin/{{default_branch}}..HEAD

Check for common issues: - Bugs: off-by-one, null handling, edge cases - Security: injection, auth bypass, exposed secrets - Style: naming, formatting, code organization - Completeness: missing error handling, incomplete paths - Cruft: debug prints, commented code, TODOs
Fix any issues found - don't just note them, fix them now
Verify no unintended changes: git diff --stat origin/{{default_branch}}...HEAD Only files relevant to the story should appear
Remove those changes

Run: gt mol step done self-review --body "## Self-Review
**Files reviewed:** [count] files, [lines] lines changed **Issues found:** [list any issues found and fixed] **Security:** [any security concerns checked] **Status:** Ready for testing"

step.goal: Run full test suite and verify coverage
step.action: Run all existing tests to ensure no regressions
Run the new tests to verify implementation correctness
Run linting and code quality checks if configured in project
Validate implementation meets ALL story acceptance criteria
STOP and fix before continuing
STOP and fix before continuing
Verify test coverage for new code: - New features should have tests - Bug fixes should have regression tests - If significant code lacks tests, add them now

Run: gt mol step done run-tests --body "## Test Results
**Test command:** [command used] **Result:** [pass count] passed, [fail count] failed **Coverage:** [new code coverage notes] **Lint/Build:** [lint and build results]"

step.goal: Ensure all implementation work is committed
step.critical: You MUST commit all changes from implementation. NEVER discard implementation work.
step.action: Check for uncommitted changes: git status
Verify clean state: git status must show "nothing to commit, working tree clean"
Verify you have commits: git log origin/{{default_branch}}..HEAD --oneline This MUST show at least 1 commit if you made changes.

Run: gt mol step done commit-changes --body "## Changes Committed
**Commits:** $(git log --oneline origin/{{default_branch}}..HEAD)
**Files changed:** $(git diff --stat origin/{{default_branch}}..HEAD)"

step.goal: Verify deployment and run acceptance tests in ephemeral environment
step.critical: Code is not complete until it works when deployed AND acceptance tests pass
step.action: Ensure all changes are committed and pushed to the remote branch: git push origin HEAD
Get current branch name: git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
Run deployment verification: scripts/verify-deployment.sh {{branch_name}} --timeout 600

check.if: verification fails due to code issue
verification fails due to infrastructure issue OR 3 consecutive verification failures
check.output: Deployment verification failed after multiple attempts. Infrastructure issue suspected.

step.action: Run acceptance tests against the ephemeral environment: make acceptance-test BRANCH={{branch_name}}
Store acceptance test output in {{acceptance_test_results}}

check.output: Deployment verification and acceptance tests passed for branch {{branch_name}}

check.if: acceptance tests fail due to code issue
acceptance tests fail due to infrastructure issue OR 3 consecutive failures
check.output: Acceptance tests failed after multiple attempts. Infrastructure issue suspected.

step.goal: Ensure workspace is pristine before handoff
step.critical: Do NOT run `git push` here. That is `gt done`'s job.
Do NOT discard implementation changes. They must already be committed.
step.action: Check for untracked files: git status --porcelain - Add to .gitignore if appropriate - Remove if temporary - Commit if needed
Check stash: git stash list (should be empty)
Verify clean state and commits: git status (must show "working tree clean") git stash list (must be empty) git log origin/{{default_branch}}..HEAD (should show your work)

check.if: git log shows nothing but you DID make changes
check.action: Something went wrong. Do NOT proceed. HALT and request guidance.

step.action:
Run: gt mol step done cleanup-workspace --body "## Workspace Clean
**Git status:** clean **Stash:** empty **Commits ahead:** $(git log --oneline origin/{{default_branch}}..HEAD | wc -l)"

step.goal: Story completion and prepare for review
step.action: Verify ALL tasks from Implementation Tasks are completed
Run the full regression suite one final time (do not skip)

Validate definition-of-done checklist: - All Implementation Tasks completed - Implementation satisfies every Acceptance Criterion from Linear issue - Unit tests for core functionality added/updated - Integration tests for component interactions added when required - End-to-end tests for critical flows added when story demands them - All tests pass (no regressions, new tests successful) - Code quality checks pass (linting, static analysis if configured) - Deployment verification passed (if applicable) - Acceptance tests passed (if applicable)
HALT - Complete remaining tasks before marking ready for review
HALT - Fix regression issues before completing
HALT - Address DoD failures before completing
Update issue notes: bd update {{issue}} --notes "Implemented: [brief summary]"
Sync beads: bd sync

Run: gt mol step done prepare-for-review --body "## Ready for Review
**Issue:** {{story_key}} **Branch:** [branch-name] **Summary:** [what was implemented] **Commits:** [count] commits **Files changed:** [count] files **Tests added:** [test summary] **Deployment:** [passed/skipped] **Acceptance tests:** [passed/skipped]"

step.critical: Once you run `gt done`, you're gone. The command pushes your branch, creates an MR bead, sets Linear to Code Complete, nukes your sandbox, and exits. Do NOT close the Linear issue - the Refinery does that after merge.
step.action: Run: gt done
